transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Park (Redwood CSM); Anika Rao (Velox SRE), Liam O'Connor (Velox CISO), Priya Menon (Velox Product), Marco Ruiz (Velox Eng)

Optional auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Velox experienced a silent degradation in streaming responses over three service windows leading to retries and client reconnects. Redwood presented a preliminary RCA focusing on the streaming aggregator + prefix handling path, proposed a short-term hotfix and longer-term orchestration/fallback mitigations. Customer requested incident timeline, sanitized traces, and SLA credit calculation. Next steps agreed include hotfix to staging, data handoff, and a canary test.

Topics: RCA walkthrough, short-term hotfix, runbook and fallback orchestration, SLA & credits, data handoff for replay, canary test scheduling.

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) --
00:00 - Maria Chen: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. Uh, we know this is a, a high-priority. We'd like to walk through our findings and get alignment on immediate remediation and the follow-up. If we can, Devon will run the short rc-a, and then we'll go through action items.
00:25 - Devon Patel: Hey all. So quick TL;DR before I, I get too into the weeds: we traced the bulk of error/retry spike to the streaming aggregator path where partial chunk reassembly + prefix trimming interacted badly with the K-V cache priming. Basically the runtime sometimes re-sent an early empty chunk and the client retried which caused session duplication, token duplication, and backpressure.
00:48 - Anika Rao: Sorry, can you say the K-V cache bit again, I think you said K dash V?
00:52 - Devon Patel: Yeah, K-V cache, our KV cache for attention state. In some cases when prefix trimming kicked in under low-memory pressure the cache pointer was not advanced before a malformed intermediate stream was acknowledged, which led to a repeated prefix being applied on the next request.
01:12 - Marco Ruiz: Right, we saw sequence repeats on our end, yeah, repeated tokens, then client reconnects. This started after your recent streaming change, right?
01:21 - Devon Patel: There's correlation with the streaming keepalive refactor we shipped two weeks ago, yes. Not a guaranteed causation but it's strongly correlated on the timelines.
01:30 - Liam O'Connor: From security standpoint, was any customer data exposed during those retransmissions?
01:34 - Maria Chen: Short answer: no sign of exfiltration. The repeated chunks were within existing sessions and didn't cross tenant boundaries. We'll include the audit log snippet in the timeline doc.
01:45 - Priya Menon: For product, our users saw duplicate responses and sometimes truncated outputs; that resulted in higher retry rates. We lost some trust on chat flows. So we need a mitigation that is low-risk to roll out.
01:58 - Devon Patel: Totally. So we proposed three tiers: immediate hotfix (server-side guard that rejects duplicate chunk sequence ids and a quick token-drop metric), staged canary with traffic-shaping and golden-run replay, and long term - orchestration-level circuit-breaker and prefix checksum.
02:22 - Anika Rao: Can you explain the "token-drop metric"?
02:26 - Devon Patel: Yeah, token-drop is a new telemetry gauge that measures when the runtime discards tokens during prefix trimming or when we detect mismatched sequence ids. It helps quantify how often the path is exercised. It's lightweight.
02:38 - Maria Chen: We'll add that to the dashboard and give you a link. (link: https://app.redwood.example.com/velox/token-drop) // note link auto-copied, may be ephemeral
02:49 - Marco Ruiz: Ok. We need something we can validate quickly. We'll need staging replay with our sanitized traffic.
02:56 - Maria Chen: Agreed. Anika, can you share the trace set? If you redact customer PII, we can replay internally and with you.
03:05 - Anika Rao: Yes, we can do that. We'll get the last 48 hours of traces and a sample payloads zip. We need an NDA addendum? Not sure.
03:15 - Jules Park: For the sanitized traces we can accept hashed IDs; no new contract should be necessary, just a secure upload link. We'll send the secure S3 upload with instructions.
03:24 - Liam O'Connor: Also we want the incident timeline and SLA impact estimate. We have a legal review next week.
03:30 - Maria Chen: We'll draft a customer-facing incident timeline and an estimate of requested SLA credits, yes.
03:36 - Devon Patel: I want to go through a quick visual of the call path. (interruption) So, on the server, when the streaming aggregator receives the first chunk it assigns a seq-id and primes KV for that session. If the prefix trimming timer runs and the chunk is small, the system trimmed and then... there was a race on pointer advancement. The pointer didn't move and the next request re-applied the same prefix.
04:06 - Marco Ruiz: So it's a pointer race, could also be GC related on the node?
04:10 - Devon Patel: We looked for GC pauses; not correlated. More likely a locking gap in the aggregator state machine under the new keepalive optimization.
04:20 - Anika Rao: Are there customers on Dedicated or Private who might see this differently?
04:24 - Maria Chen: Dedicated customers with pinned model versions saw it depending on whether they had the keepalive refactor applied; private deployments that had older runtimes did not exhibit the issue.
04:35 - Priya Menon: What's our rollback threshold if the hotfix causes a regression?
04:38 - Devon Patel: Hotfix is a guard only; it should be safe to enable/disable via feature flag. We'll ship it to staging behind a flag and can revert instantly.
04:46 - Liam O'Connor: About data retention — can you also include the audit logs for admin actions during the incident window?
04:51 - Maria Chen: Yes, audit logs and SSO events. We'll bundle SOC 2 relevant artifacts in the security appendix. (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/packet/velox)
05:05 - Devon Patel: Quick note on the long-term fix: we recommend adding a prefix checksum and sequence id monotonic validator at the RPC layer plus an orchestrated fallback that can route to a compatible model variant or reduce sequence length. That reduces blast radius rather than just patching the symptom.
05:26 - Marco Ruiz: Would that require model changes or just runtime changes?
05:29 - Devon Patel: Runtime only. Checksum and seq validator are in the inference runtime and gateway. No model retrain needed.
05:36 - Anika Rao: For the canary, what size of traffic are you proposing?
05:40 - Devon Patel: We suggest a 5% shaded canary for 30 minutes with golden-run replays and live telemetry watching token-drop, lat p95, and error-rates. If that looks clean, bump to 20% for 2 hours.
05:56 - Priya Menon: We also need a customer-visible fallback message strategy; in some flows we rather show degraded UI than duplicate responses.
06:04 - Maria Chen: Good point. We'll provide a suggested UX fallback text and API error code mapping so your front-end can degrade gracefully.
06:13 - Liam O'Connor: One more ask — can you provide a deterministic way to map a request id to internal session id for us to validate traces?
06:20 - Devon Patel: We can expose a request mapping token — hashed pointer — in the debug trace bundle. We'll include instructions on how to map safely without exposing raw tokens.
06:29 - (short crosstalk) Speaker 1: mm-hmm, ok, yeah
06:34 - Maria Chen: Alright, I want to walk through the timeline we intend to send. Devon— can you summarize a minimal timeline text?
06:40 - Devon Patel: Sure— Initial anomaly observed at 2027-01-07 03:20 UTC with elevated stream retry rate; on-call noticed increase and escalated; on 01-08 we rolled a keepalive optimization (internal rollout); 01-09 to 01-10 we saw sporadic repeats; 01-10 22:00 we triggered a broader alert and started tracing; 01-11 mitigation work started and hotfix draft under test. We'll send a clean timeline with exact logs and signal artifacts.
07:12 - Anika Rao: Please include the exact timestamps in our local timezone too (PST).
07:15 - Maria Chen: Will do.
07:18 - Marco Ruiz: About the billing / SLA — we expect Redwood to calculate the credit based on the impacted window and p99 S-L-A.
07:25 - Jules Park: On the billing side, I'll open ticket with billing and include the impact metrics. We'll also escalate to the account exec if it looks like a multi-week impact.
07:36 - Liam O'Connor: Are there any privacy/regulatory kudos here? We operate in EU too.
07:40 - Maria Chen: We'll include region-specific audit slices and note any cross-region routing. No PII was leaked per initial checks.
07:47 - Devon Patel: Technical deep dive quick path — two additional anomalies: 1) intermittent socket close with 100ms jitter that correlated with the repeated chunk, 2) a small percentage of requests saw the aggregator replay older cache frames when the session id reused across backends.
08:10 - Priya Menon: The second one worries us. Could it cause cross-tenant leakage?
08:14 - Devon Patel: No, we audited tenant isolation boundaries; the cache frames were tenant-scoped, but the confusion was within a single tenant session due to seq-id duplication, not cross-tenant.
08:24 - Anika Rao: Ok. We'll still want to see the audit that verifies no cross-tenant events.
08:29 - Devon Patel: Yep, included in the appendix.
08:33 - (pause)
08:40 - Maria Chen: Let's talk risk windows for the hotfix deployment. We want to minimize client impact. Proposed plan: deploy to staging, run 12h soak, then a 30-min 5% canary with Velox traffic window; if green, widen. Rollback on any p95 latency regression > 15% or token-drop increase > 30% within canary.
09:05 - Marco Ruiz: That sounds reasonable. What about on-prem/private deployments?
09:09 - Devon Patel: Private customers will get a patch release; we can provide the hotfix as a patch and if you want we can coordinate with your infra team for an out-of-band deployment. It won't auto-update your private runtime.
09:22 - Marco Ruiz: We'll probably schedule that.
09:25 - Anika Rao: We need realistic SLAs for the canary. Can you guarantee rollback window?
09:30 - Maria Chen: We'll outline a strict rollback playbook and include owners/contacts.
09:34 - Liam O'Connor: On the legal front, we may request a formal credit. Who will compute the impact?
09:38 - Jules Park: Jules will coordinate with billing and your procurement contact to compute the impacted tokens and estimate credits. We'll include that in the incident timeline doc.
09:46 - (15s of side conversation about spreadsheets and a link)
10:05 - Maria Chen: I'll attach the benchmark & impact sheet here: https://redwood.example.com/internal/velox-impact (access controlled).
10:12 - Priya Menon: We also want a runbook rewrite so our SREs can recognize the pattern and escalate.
10:18 - Devon Patel: We'll provide a short runbook: detection thresholds, console grep commands, and a mitigation toggle. We'll push it to your shared Confluence.
10:28 - Anika Rao: And a play to rotate the session keys?
10:31 - Devon Patel: Not necessary now; it's unrelated. But we will include session mapping steps for investigation.
10:38 - Maria Chen: Alright, let's surface what we expect to deliver within 24 hours: hotfix candidate, internal staging results, customer-facing timeline, secure upload link for traces. Anything missing?
10:50 - Anika Rao: Please include the debug mapping token and the data retention slice for our legal team.
10:54 - Maria Chen: Noted.
10:58 - Marco Ruiz: What about the longer-term plan and ETA?
11:01 - Devon Patel: For the orchestration-level changes (prefix checksum + seq validator + fallback) estimated 6-8 weeks for dev + testing + staged rollout. We'll treat that as a roadmap item with priority.
11:13 - Priya Menon: Ok would like visibility into that roadmap milestone.
11:16 - Maria Chen: We'll add the milestone to the quarterly roadmap doc and share weekly status until resolved.
11:24 - Liam O'Connor: Can you confirm whether any other customers reported similar symptoms?
11:28 - Devon Patel: A handful of Hosted customers with the keepalive refactor enabled saw small blips but none at the same scale as Velox; Dedicated/private where runtime older did not. We'll provide an anonymized prevalence report.
11:42 - (brief cross-talk)
11:50 - Jules Park: On the support side, we'll set up a dedicated slack channel and a daily 9am PST check-in until we close the pilot. I'll send invites after the call.
11:58 - Anika Rao: Good.
12:03 - Maria Chen: Any other immediate concerns from the customer side?
12:07 - Priya Menon: Just that we retain a single owner for the timeline — our procurement needs it packaged.
12:10 - Maria Chen: Maria will be the owner; Jules will carry the billing thread.
12:14 - Marco Ruiz: We also want a small proof of mitigation before we tell our customers it's fixed.
12:18 - Devon Patel: Understandable. Staging soak + 30m 5% canary with your live traffic should be sufficient proof.
12:27 - (short pause)
12:33 - Liam O'Connor: One last technical thing — you mentioned a prefix checksum. Is that computationally heavy? Could it add latency?
12:38 - Devon Patel: No, it's tiny — a 64-bit rolling checksum on the prefix bytes, computed incrementally. We do have to ensure it's on the fast-path; throughput penalty is negligible in tests (<1% p50).
12:51 - Anika Rao: Ok, sounds good.
12:54 - Maria Chen: Quick recap of action items: Devon will push the hotfix candidate and token-drop metric to staging; Maria will draft the timeline and SLA calc; Jules will open billing ticket; Anika will upload sanitized traces. We'll reconvene after staging soak or sooner if anything urgent.
13:18 - Marco Ruiz: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
13:21 - Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll email the timeline and the secure upload link in the next 3 hours.
13:28 - Priya Menon: Thanks all.
13:30 - (meeting ends)
